pages.text: Luna is the Moon. She is Earth’s closest space friend and follows Earth wherever it goes.
Luna is not a star. She does not make her own light. She shines by reflecting light from the Sun.
Luna travels around Earth in a path called an orbit. She goes all the way around again and again.
As Luna moves, we see different shapes of her. These shapes are called Moon phases.
Sometimes Luna looks full and round. Sometimes she looks like a tiny glowing slice.
Luna’s gentle pull helps move ocean water. This movement makes tides go in and out.
At night, Luna lights the sky. She helps us see softly when the Sun is sleeping.
Luna stays close to Earth. She does not float away, because Earth’s gravity keeps her nearby.
People have visited Luna. Astronauts walked on her rocky surface long ago.
At bedtime, we remember: Luna orbits Earth, shines with sunlight, and changes her shape in the sky.
